candidates.name: Tom Cotton
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2015, seeking a third term; chairs the Senate Intelligence Committee. Harvard Law graduate and U.S. Army veteran who deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan and earned a Bronze Star. Served one House term before the Senate. Won the March 3 Republican primary with about 82%.
priorities: Rebuild the military and confront China

immigration.label: Co-sponsored the RAISE Act to cut family-based immigration and cap refugees at 50,000; 'We cannot afford to grant illegal aliens amnesty or a so-called earned path to citizenship' (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Championed the 2017 tax-cut bill; his individual-mandate repeal 'will pay for a lot more tax cuts for working families' (Senate office)

safety.label: Wrote the 'Send in the Troops' op-ed on 2020 protests; opposed the First Step Act, saying the U.S. has an 'under-incarceration problem' (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Called Roe v. Wade a 'tragic mistake'; voted for the 20-week Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: At a March 2021 press conference on election security with Sen. Boozman, blasted 'legislation backed by Democrats to nationalize U.S. elections and enact radical changes to our voting system' (Boozman-Cotton release)

climate.label: Voted yea on H.J.Res. 88, disapproving California's EPA waiver for its EV/clean-car sales mandate (senate.gov roll vote 277, May 22, 2025)

education.label: Parents, not politicians and bureaucrats, know what is best for their children, advocates for home schooling, charter schools, and private and religious schools (cotton.senate.gov National School Choice Week statement)

candidates.name: Jeffrey Francis Wadlin
candidates.now: Businessman and management consultant; Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate
candidates.background: Wadlin is a Bentonville businessman with a mechanical engineering degree from the University of Virginia and an MBA from Northwestern University, whose career includes roles at Caterpillar, Capital One, and Sam's Club before starting his own consulting business. He won the Libertarian Party of Arkansas's 2026 U.S. Senate nomination and describes himself as a centrist offering "pragmatic solutions."

cost.label: Says Arkansas's middle class "is being squeezed" and calls for "pragmatic, results driven reforms" on cost and wages "rather than government dependency programs" (Arkansas Times)

sources.label: Arkansas Times: Libertarian U.S. Senate candidate announces campaign kickoff
